documents.unit: University Policy 3710.2: Academic Integrity Standards and Process for Misconduct
documents.title: Academic Integrity Standards and Process for Misconduct (generative AI provisions)
documents.stance_why: Section 3710.2 sets a university default that bans AI: 'If an AI statement is not included in the course syllabus... students may not use any type of generative AI', yet it also says 'Instructors are free to establish their own additional protocols... allowing or disallowing some or all use'. It sets a university-wide default ban that instructors can lift by syllabus statement, so AI is banned unless explicitly permitted, which is restrict. It is not delegates, because the silent-syllabus default is a binding ban with misconduct consequences, and it offers no tiers.
documents.summary: The generative-AI section (3710.2) of Wright State's academic-integrity policy defines generative AI, bans its use on coursework unless the syllabus or instructor permits it, and treats unauthorized use as an integrity violation. Instructors may allow or disallow use if they say so in the syllabus, and students who are unsure should ask. The rest of the policy is the general misconduct process and sanctions that AI cases follow.

units.why: The section defines generative AI as 'any type of software... capable of creating, writing, or re-writing any form of content', which sets what the policy covers, so it is a definition (P61), informs, phase general.
units.anchor: any type of software, i.e. algorithm, that is capable of creating, writing, or re-writing
units.resolution_why: Both coders: P61, informs, general, all. Topics differed (A policy-evolution, B default-stance); a scope definition does not state the default stance, so policy-evolution is kept.

units.why: 'Generative AI tools are distinct from search engines in that they generate content' draws the scope boundary between generative AI and search, which is a scope definition (P61) rather than a rule.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools are distinct from search engines in that they generate content
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on P61/informs/general; topics differed, kept A's.

units.why: 'Submitting content created by any of the above means, either in its original or edited form, will constitute use of generative AI' fixes that edited AI output still counts as AI use; it is a scope rule (P61) and not a ban.
units.anchor: either in its original or edited form, will constitute use of generative AI
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on P61 and student; B added fit_note and topic prohibited-uses. The sentence defines what counts as AI use, so P61 stays and the fit_note is kept.
units.fit_note: Also states that lightly edited AI output still counts as generative AI use, which is a scoping rule about submissions more than a definition of AI.

units.why: Gives the reason assignments develop 'the student's voice and perspective' and AI 'may be undermined': AI shortcuts the practice that builds the skill (P41), not a fairness or career argument.

units.fit_note: Rationale is tied to reflective, research and interpretive assignments, not to coding practice. Also says affected work "will be graded accordingly", an unspecified grading consequence (coded separately).
units.resolution_why: Both coders: P41, informs, restrict. A split 'graded accordingly' into a separate unit. The rationale unit is kept with the fit_note; the grading consequence is kept as its own unit.

units.why: 'will be graded accordingly' warns that AI use in voice-developing assignments is reflected in the grade, a consequence stated in advance but with no specific penalty; P37 is the nearest type, though it is vague, so I note the fit.

units.fit_note: No concrete penalty is stated, only that the work 'will be graded accordingly' because AI undermines its purpose.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this as a separate unit (B folded it into the P41 fit_note). Source: 'may be undermined and will be graded accordingly' is a stated grading consequence without a concrete penalty, so it is a real statement; P37 is the nearest type, kept with its fit_note. Phase during-work (assignments), modality informs.

units.why: 'Instructors are free to establish their own additional protocols... including allowing or disallowing some or all use' hands the decision to each instructor (P04), a delegation rather than a university rule.

units.why: Instructor protocols must be 'consistent with applicable University policies, including those on academic standards and conduct' and IP attribution; this is a duty to comply with existing university policy and law (P77).

units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on P77, must, instructor; B added integrity-sanctions topic. Source: protocols must be consistent with university policies on academic standards and conduct and IP attribution; kept IP and instructor-discretion.

units.why: Instructors who allow AI must 'incorporate protocols into their course syllabi and/or course content' and 'expressly communicate how this technology may be used', a syllabus-statement duty (P09). It binds only instructors who allow AI, which the fit note records.

units.fit_note: The duty applies only to instructors who allow AI; instructors who ban it are not required to state it, because the default already bans.
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on P09, must, course-start, with the same fit_note. unit_stance: A permit, B neutral; the duty binds instructors who allow AI and sets no position itself, so neutral.

units.why: 'If an AI statement is not included in the course syllabus... then students may not use any type of generative AI' is the fallback when the syllabus is silent (P06), and it is a ban, so must-not.

units.policy: When an AI statement is not included in the course syllabus and/or course content, students may not use any type of generative AI to complete coursework.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P06, student, must-not. Phase: A general, B during-work. Source: students 'may not use any type of generative AI to complete coursework', a rule on doing the work, so during-work. unit_stance: A prohibit, B restrict; the ban is a default that the syllabus can lift, so restrict. B's anchor/policy null; A's normalized policy kept because the anchor alone omits the syllabus condition.

units.why: 'Using generative AI to complete any assignment or exam... without express permission from the instructor, will constitute an academic integrity violation' classes unauthorized AI as misconduct (P36).

units.why: The ban covers 'any assignment or exam, or any portion thereof', so AI on exams is covered too (P22); I chose P22 for the exam reach and P36 for the misconduct unit above.

units.why: 'Students who are unsure... are encouraged to ask their instructor for clarification' is the ask-first rule (P10), should modality.

units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P10, student, should. Phase: A course-start, B during-work. Source: students unsure of 'policies or protocols' are encouraged to ask the instructor, which concerns learning the course expectations, so course-start.

units.why: 'the instructor must carefully review the content for signs of such use' sets how suspected AI misuse is identified: by instructor review, not a tool. It is detection by evidence (P40 nearest), and the fit note says no tool is named.

units.fit_note: Requires careful instructor review of the content but does not say what evidence suffices; no software, commit history or logs are named.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor/phase/modality (instructor, when-misuse, must) but differed on type: A P40, B P69. P40 requires a named tool or log (similarity checks, detectors, commit histories); the source names none, only careful review of the content. P69 covers the kinds of evidence to weigh, so P69 with B's fit_note plus A's note that no tool is named.

units.why: 'based on the instructor's subject matter expertise and discretion' sets the evidence basis for a finding of AI use as the instructor's judgment, which is an evidence standard (P69).

notes: Only section 3710.2 (AI) is coded. Coder A also coded 9 units from 3710.3-3710.6 (general integrity reporting, meeting, hearing, sanctions); the source passages do not mention AI, so they were dropped as general boilerplate per the codebook, consistent with coder B. Course layer deferred. The 2023 AI committee report was excluded as superseded.
